title: evening-ops-escalation-checklist-2026-03-26
body:
Purpose: quick handoff + escalation digest for evening shift. High-level: short, messy — intended for the next oncall to pick up and follow the TODOs/ask calls.

Summary (TL;DR):
- 18:07 UTC: Production p95 generation latency spike observed against hosted-api-prod (route: /v1/generate). p95 jumped to ~1.9s from baseline ~140ms for ~22 minutes.
- Root-cause (probable): Large model variant rollout to a new dedicated pool combined with cold KV cache (cache-miss surge) + a transient autoscaler cooldown preventing immediate scale-up.
- Impact: consumer-facing latency increased; no error rate spike above 1% but request queue length increased on 3 replica pods. A handful of internal jobs (batch embedding churn) exacerbated resource contention.
- Current status: mitigations applied, latency stabilized ~200ms after manual steps. Follow-ups and runbook edits pending.

Timeline + actions (concise):
- 18:03: Alert: p95_gen > 800ms for 5m (PagerDuty).
- 18:07: Investigated tracing — traces show increased total_decode_time and more KV-cache-miss traces (tag: cache_status=miss).
- 18:09: Confirmed a canary rollout for model-id: redwood-opt-7b-v2 to dedicated-pool-eu-west started at 18:00 (deploy pipeline #PR-7446). Canary weight ~30%.
- 18:11: Observed autoscaler (pool:d-exec-eu) not scaling instantly due to cooldown window (set to 10m). Node CPU at ~82% on three nodes; queue depth rising.
- 18:12: Temporarily paused canary (rolled back canary weight to previous variant) — partial rollback applied by Miguel.
- 18:14: Triggered manual scale-out: increased desired replicas from 4 -> 8 in pool config to relieve queue.
- 18:16: Enabled temporary KV warmup job (internal endpoint /internal/cache-warmup) to prime prefix caches for the canary traffic shape.
- 18:21: Observed p95 falling toward 220–300ms; queue cleared by 18:25.
- 18:30: Postmortem note captured in JIRA-5892, initial draft of incident blameless timeline created.

Immediate mitigation checklist (what I did):
- paused canary rollout
- manual scaleout of dedicated pool
- triggered cache warmup script against canary model variants
- notified product/infra via #prod-ops and paging channel
- opened JIRA-5892 and linked traces

Things that helped:
- tracing metadata with cache_status tag allowed quick correlation
- the ability to manually scale dedicated pools is effective (but slow during cooldown)

Gaps observed / why this happened:
- autoscaler cooldown is too aggressive for canary rollouts; cooling window prevented rapid reactive scale-up during sudden traffic pattern change.
- no alarm for high cache-miss rates (we only alert on latency/error). Miss rate rose to ~38% for 10m — should be an SLA signal or early warning.
- cache warmup mechanism exists but is not wired to automated post-deploy hooks for large model switches.
- dedicated pool instance types were constrained by a max-per-zone cap; we hit soft limits and scaling required manual override.

Follow-ups / action items (owners assigned where obvious):
- (Eng-infra) Reduce autoscaler cooldown or add a short-term emergency override trigger for canary rollouts — ticket JIRA-5901 (owner: Rina).
- (SRE) Add alert: "kv_cache_miss_rate > 25% for 5m" and tie to a runbook to either warm or temporarily route traffic to warmed variant — ticket JIRA-5899 (owner: Daniel).
- (Platform) Add cache-warmup hook to rollout pipeline when model size > 4B or when canary weight >= 20% — ticket JIRA-5905 (owner: Miguel).
- (SRE/Runbooks) Draft a short runbook: when p95 > 600ms + cache_miss_rate > 20% -> pause rollout, warm cache, scaleout pool, monitor for 10m before resume. Put draft in Confluence and link: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SRE/kv-cache-warmup-runbook (owner: Daniel).
- (Capacity) Verify soft quotas in eu-west zone; request quota bump if needed (owner: infra-capacity team).
- (Observability) Add quick dashboard tile for cache_miss_rate by model and pool (owner: observability team).

Runbook draft snippet (copy this into Confluence runbook entry - lean):
- Trigger conditions: p95_gen > 600ms for 5m AND kv_cache_miss_rate > 20% for 5m / OR sustained queue_depth > 50 for 3m.
- Immediate steps: (1) Pause rollout (if currently rolling), (2) scale dedicated pool +30% desired replicas (manual or via emergency override), (3) start cache warmup against latest model bin (endpoint /internal/cache-warmup?model=<id>&rate=50r/s for 3m), (4) monitor p95 and queue for 10m, (5) if stable, resume rollout at reduced weight.
- Post-incident: open ticket to automate step (3) in rollout.

Notes for incoming shift:
- Next watch window: 20:00-03:00 UTC; likely to see more traffic from APAC ramp. Keep an eye on pool:d-exec-eu and pool:d-exec-apac.
- Quick checks on start: p95_gen, kv_cache_miss_rate, queue_depth_by_pool, node_cpu.
- If you see p95 creep: first check cache_miss tag in traces — that's the fastest signal.
- If pager fires for p95 > 800ms, follow runbook snippet above.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we add a passive traffic splitter that routes a small percentage to a warmed region to reduce blast radius? (Product input needed)
- How to balance warming cost vs latency savings for small models used intermittently? (ops + product discussion)

Miscellaneous smaller items encountered:
- One sidecar in pod svc-gen-7 crashed at 18:10 due to OOM; restarted automatically. Filetered in logs as sidecar OOM; not the primary cause but worth checking memory requests for sidecars.
- Observed higher-than-normal retry counts from internal batch embedding job at 17:50–18:00; ticketed to infra-team to investigate job scheduling overlap (JIRA-5900).

Suggested messaging for customer comms (if needed):
- For small latency blips like this, we can send a short status update: "We observed elevated latency affecting a subset of requests between 18:05–18:25 UTC due to an internal model rollout combined with cache warmup. Service is restored; investigating long-term mitigations." Keep wording non-technical.

Handoff checklist for you (next oncall):
- Read JIRA-5892 (incident draft) and append any missing trace links.
- Kick off JIRA-5899 if you agree with the new alert thresholds.
- Verify the autoscaler cooldown change progress on JIRA-5901; escalate to infra manager if blocked.
- Keep the cache-warmup automation ticket on the radar (JIRA-5905) — that will prevent repetition.

Contacts (people paged / messaged):
- Miguel Alvarez (platform lead) — worked rollback and warmup
- Rina Patel (infra) — checking autoscaler cooldown/limits
- Aisha Rahman (obs) — will add dashboard and alert

Quick links:
- Incident draft: JIRA-5892
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SRE/kv-cache-warmup-runbook
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/trace-2026-03-26-1807
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SRE/p1679882345678

End of notes. Short, messy, direct. Ping me (DM) if you need context for the cache_warmup script or to walk through the scale steps.

— Daniel
